interest: Offers rich contemporaneous insight into Japan's militarization and international isolation in 1933, pairing granular Embassy Tokyo field reports with State Department Far Eastern Affairs analytical memoranda covering the May 15 trials, coup plots, Chinese Eastern Railway talks, and trade disputes.
overview: Comprising Part 2 of State Department File 822 (Decimal File 894.00, Political Affairs in Japan), this collection of 419 pages and 26 documents spans March through October 1933. It centers on Embassy Tokyo's comprehensive monthly political reports compiled under Ambassador Joseph C. Grew alongside analytical summary memoranda prepared by the State Department's Division of Far Eastern Affairs. The file thoroughly documents Japan's internal and external affairs during a pivotal transition: domestically, the erosion of constitutional party governance under the Saito Cabinet, the trials of the May 15 and League of Blood assassins, newly thwarted ultranationalist plots like the 'God-Sent Troops', defense budget struggles led by Finance Minister Takahashi, and the restructuring of the Naval General Staff; internationally, Japan's formal withdrawal from the League of Nations, military actions and truce in North China, negotiations over the Chinese Eastern Railway, commercial frictions over cotton with Great Britain and India, and the diplomatic impact of the appointment of Foreign Minister Koki Hirota amid American naval expansion and Soviet-American rapprochement.
